title: An Unconventional Conglomerateur
coreMove: Separate the permanent scorecard from the temporary instrument, then change instruments when facts and valuation change.
sourcePressure: Henry Singleton and Teledyne demonstrate fixed loyalty to per-share value while tactics shift from equity-funded acquisitions to large repurchases as valuation and market conditions change.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not treat Singleton as randomly contrarian; every example must show a stable value standard and a changed tool under changed facts.

sourceAnchors.name: Henry Singleton
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies Chapter 2 as Henry Singleton and Teledyne and says he should be judged by per-share value rather than size or earnings growth.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Henry Singleton looks strange only until per-share value becomes the ruler on the table.

sourceAnchors.name: I change my mind when the facts change. What do you do?
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says the visible chapter header includes this exact quote.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The line about changing his mind when facts change is not a shrug; it is the discipline of moving the tool while keeping the ruler.

sourceAnchors.name: institutional imperative
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar names the institutional imperative as the tendency of managers to favor scale and convention over unconventional value creation.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The institutional imperative is the room pressure that makes a bad respectable choice feel safer than a good odd one.

hook: The odd choice is often right
counterintuition: Buybacks are always smarter than acquisitions
examples: investment club using last semester rule
family savings plan from legacy draft
any scene where buybacks become personal budgeting literally

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: No more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'.
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: At least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human.
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: farm-equipment rental cooperative revising purchase rules after used prices spike
exampleSpecs.audience: a cooperative treasurer loyal to last year's fleet expansion rule
exampleSpecs.stakes: members need harvest reliability but resale prices now make repair capacity more valuable than new units
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: David writes last year's rule and this year's auction prices on the same maintenance bay door, then shifts capital from buying tractors to rebuilding engines because the per-member uptime math changed.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: mud drying on the tire of a rental tractor beside chalked auction prices

exampleSpecs.domain: Paris subscription news app deciding between user growth and churn reduction
exampleSpecs.audience: a product lead pressured to keep chasing headline subscriber counts
exampleSpecs.stakes: new signups look good while paid retention erodes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Camille asks the room to predict value per paying user after the discount campaign, then reveals the cohort table and kills the growth tactic that now dilutes the scorecard.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cohort-retention table reflected in a dark conference screen
mustAvoid: startup growth cliche without per-share logic

exampleSpecs.domain: regional hospital foundation shifting donor strategy after tax law changes
exampleSpecs.audience: a foundation director who used to favor gala sponsorships
exampleSpecs.stakes: funding a pediatric ultrasound suite before the fiscal year closes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Jonas places the old gala return sheet beside the new planned-giving memo and changes the fundraising instrument while keeping the same equipment target.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: silver name badges left in a tray after the donor gala

exampleSpecs.domain: artisan furniture workshop choosing wholesale channels after lumber costs reverse
exampleSpecs.audience: a shop owner proud of last year's direct-to-consumer rule
exampleSpecs.stakes: cash tied in inventory while margins shift underneath the old doctrine
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Three inventory counts later, Chiara separates the margin target from the sales-channel rule and moves selected pieces through wholesale because facts made the old channel weaker.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: walnut boards stacked under a handwritten cost tag
mustAvoid: craft passion versus business discipline trope

exampleSpecs.domain: university lab deciding whether to lease or buy specialized imaging equipment
exampleSpecs.audience: a principal investigator defending the lab's old ownership rule
exampleSpecs.stakes: grant money expires while machine utilization drops
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You see Andrew mark the utilization hours against lease rates and admit the ownership rule once made sense, then switch to leasing without treating the old rule as a betrayal.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a calibration slide glowing under a microscope lamp
mustAvoid: school club example from legacy draft

exampleSpecs.domain: London food importer deciding between warehouse expansion and supplier prepayments
exampleSpecs.audience: a finance head under board pressure to look decisive after a strong year
exampleSpecs.stakes: currency swings can erase the margin before shipments arrive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Which move still serves gross margin after sterling moves? Layla walks the board from warehouse expansion to supplier prepayments because the facts changed while the margin standard did not.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a currency hedge confirmation beside a dock arrival notice

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: distinguish changing methods from abandoning the standard
identify institutional pressure toward respectable but weaker choices
apply per-unit or per-owner value logic outside public-company finance
evaluate when a former rule has become ritual consistency

tryThisNowSpec: Name one tactic you are still defending, then write the unchanged scorecard it was meant to serve and one fact that would justify replacing the tactic.
